assessment.answer: The score sits in the 0.5-0.7 band mainly because annualized net income (-$159.6M, -18.4% of assets) and operating income (-$150.4M) are deeply negative, and current assets are only 11.4% of total assets (10th peer percentile), giving a current ratio of 0.66 against a peer median of 1.42. The filings explain most of this. About 93% of the six-month loss is non-cash, mostly stock compensation (much of it in Q1) and depreciation, so annualizing the half-year overstates the cash loss, which is only -$5.5M for the six months. The real pressure is liquidity: cash fell from $274.1M to $90.0M, mainly because of Lake Mariner capex and buybacks. There is no debt due before February 2030, and $200M of ATM capacity remains, so the risk looks close to the band's base rate rather than clearly above it.
